prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1273; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss by phone from the insured driver. Reports a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. Other vehicle reportedly drifted into the insured's lane. Insured reports neck and back pain at scene and was transported to urgent care. Photos of both vehicles requested. Policy confirmed active and coverage reviewed for collision and bodily injury liability.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant's attorney's office. Counsel confirmed representation and asked that all communication go through their firm. Requested the claimant's medical records and the treating provider list. Advised that the property damage estimate will follow once the vehicle is inspected. Noted the attorney's preference for written correspondence.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. It lists the other driver as cited for failure to maintain lane. Both drivers gave statements at the scene that are consistent with the sideswipe. No independent witnesses identified so far. Canvass of nearby businesses for dashcam or security footage is pending.

Entry 4: Received the claimant's treatment summary from the physical therapy clinic. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain with limited range of motion. Treatment plan calls for twelve weeks of therapy and a follow-up with an orthopedic provider. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the anticipated course of care. Forwarded the summary to the bodily injury examiner.

Entry 5: Attorney's office sent a demand package requesting settlement for the bodily injury claim. Package includes medical bills, a wage loss letter, and a narrative from the treating physician. Reviewing the documentation against the policy limits and the liability position before responding. Scheduled a peer review of the treatment records and set a response deadline on the file diary.
